tests/integration/conftest.py:39-40 says of MYSQL_URL = "mysql+pymysql://u@db.invalid/shop": "An unresolvable host: a real connect to it fails the same way on every machine." This is an absolute claim; the property rests entirely on name resolution, which is a property of each machine, not of the repo. Falsifying input traced: a machine where db.invalid resolves (hosts-file entry, search domain, or an NXDOMAIN-rewriting resolver). Where the name resolves, the connect proceeds to the answered address and fails differently: an immediate resolution error becomes a refused connection, a wait of up to the connect timeout, or an authentication error. In sql_runner.py the raised pymysql error text differs per case, since only preflight.py:147-150 flattens it to 'OperationalError: connection failed'. So the 'same way on every machine' guarantee is not enforced by the code and is false on such machines. Only a conforming resolver (RFC 2606 .invalid) gives the uniform outcome. The claim is source_authored, so FAIL rests on a counterexample in the authored comment, not on a requirement. No rejection covers this: the only rejections line concerns tests/unit/test_safety.py pragma_ rows. Impact is limited to an overstated comment. Base tests/unit/test_safety_table_shorthand.py:15 has DIALECTS=['mysql','sqlite',None]; head line 15 is ['mysql', None]. The two parametrized tests (test_table_shorthand_is_found, test_other_sql_is_not_flagged) assert one fixed outcome per sql string for every dialect, so expected outcomes are identical across sqlite and mysql by construction. uses_table_shorthand (src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py:79-121) has no sqlite-keyed branch: it only calls Dialect.get_or_raise(dialect).tokenize(sql) and scans for TokenType.TABLE tokens, with previous-token text (case-folded) checked against _TABLE_KEYWORD_NOT_SHORTHAND_AFTER, and quoted IDENTIFIER/STRING tokens resetting previous. I also compared the installed sqlglot tokenizers (.venv sqlglot/dialects/sqlite.py:32-54, mysql.py:87-101, tokens.py:404,533-547) against each case. 'TABLE' is a base keyword in both with no override. sqlite differs from mysql only by double-quote identifiers vs strings, '[..]' identifiers, hex strings, MATCH/ATTACH/REPLACE-as-command. Double-quoted cases ('SELECT "table" FROM t', 'FROM "table"', 'FROM "create" TABLE users') are IDENTIFIER under sqlite and STRING under mysql, but both count as quoted, so the outcomes are the same. EXPLAIN is a COMMAND under sqlite, so the rest is swallowed into a string token, and a DESCRIBE token under mysql, where previous='EXPLAIN' exempts TABLE; both give not-flagged. SHOW is swallowed as a command in both. The None dialect still covers the base double-quote-identifier tokenization. No case has a sqlite-specific outcome, so dropping sqlite removes only duplicate cases. The installed sqlglot is the .venv copy in the issue-381 worktree, not a supplied dependency_sources directory, and I did not run the tests.
